result.title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
result.summary: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision. Experiments on seven benchmarks across vision, language, speech, and medical imaging show consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/davelee-uestc/chord_debiasing_public .

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CHORD 多视图去偏框架，利用多个表示空间中的类内划分作为候选偏置的代理，在无偏置监督下通过跨视图共识修正目标表示与分类器，并在视觉、语言、语音和医学影像七个基准上提升最差组准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线仅间接相关：其「某特征空间中被遮蔽的偏置在另一空间更清晰」的跨视图一致性与分歧思路，可能可供核查用于多种 latent 假设间的证据筛选与不一致检测，但原文未涉及推理期状态生成或视觉证据使用，迁移性存疑。
